claim_text: Spare parts lead times 6–12 weeks from Indian OEM (or Chinese OEM) HQ to SEA end users
original_source: coalbiomassboiler.com/industrial-boiler-spare-parts-delivery/ (vendor blog — Taishan Group, Chinese boiler OEM)
verdict_explanation: The 6–12 week figure in the original claim is directionally plausible and partially corroborated by independent commercial data points — but no government, multilateral, academic, or formal trade press source for SEA-specific OEM-to-end-user lead times was found. The figure is consistent with part-type-specific data from a North American OEM parts retailer (York Shipley refractory: 11–13 weeks ARO) and a US trade magazine noting watertube boilers at 50-week new-unit lead time (implying custom pressure part fabrication timeframes of comparable magnitude). The vendor-blog source's own breakdown is internally consistent and is the only source that actually disaggregates by part type with specific week ranges.

supporting_evidence.key_data: York Shipley / Donlee refractory boiler parts (target rings, liner tiles, chamber tiles, rear door refractory) listed with estimated lead time of 11–13 weeks ARO (after receipt of order). This is a North American OEM parts direct-sale page, not an Indian/Chinese OEM to SEA transaction, but the fabrication-time component (cast refractory, fired tiles) is comparable regardless of geography.
supporting_evidence.reliability: medium — commercial page, but OEM direct-sale with stated lead time

supporting_evidence.key_data: Nationwide Boiler cites 'lead times for large watertube boilers now stretching to 50 weeks' for new-unit procurement as the pain point their in-stock program addresses. While this is for complete new boilers, not spare parts, it indicates that custom fabricated pressure parts (which use the same shop capacity) carry multi-week lead times as an industry baseline.
supporting_evidence.reliability: low-medium — industry marketing blog, US context

supporting_evidence.key_data: Article by Taishan Group (Chinese biomass/coal boiler OEM, sells to SEA) provides part-type breakdown: gaskets 1–3 business days; custom burners 2–6 weeks; control panels 4–8 weeks; pressure vessel sections 6–12 weeks; custom tube bundles 4–10 weeks; boiler shell or drum sections 8–14 weeks. Does NOT provide origin-specific (India/China to SEA) data — generic 'overseas OEM' framing only.
supporting_evidence.reliability: low — vendor blog, self-interest in communicating challenge to sell spare-parts service

key_gap: No primary source (government customs data, port authority statistics, OEM investor disclosure, or peer-reviewed study) was found that directly quantifies spare parts transit + manufacture lead time from India or Chinese OEM HQ to SEA end user in weeks. The SEA-specific dimension of the claim (cross-border shipping + customs clearance component) remains unsourced by any authoritative data.

suggested_revision.revised_claim_text: Spare parts lead times from Indian or Chinese industrial boiler OEMs to SEA end users typically range 4–14 weeks depending on part type: consumables and gaskets 1–2 weeks (in-stock items + sea freight); control panels and custom burners 4–8 weeks; pressure parts (waterwall panels, superheater sections) 8–14 weeks (custom fabrication + shipping). Refractory tiles from OEM stock carry 11–13 week ARO lead times even for North American OEM direct-sale; for SEA cross-border orders add 2–4 weeks customs and inland freight.
suggested_revision.citation_guidance: Retain coalbiomassboiler.com for the part-type table; add York Shipley ARO data point as independent corroboration for refractory specifically; mark the overall range as [FIELD-VALIDATE] pending operator interviews in Indonesia/Malaysia/Vietnam.
suggested_revision.rationale: The directional range 6–12 weeks for non-consumable pressure parts is plausible and corroborated by one independent OEM parts page for the comparable fabrication category (refractory: 11–13 weeks). The SEA cross-border shipping premium above domestic US/India timelines adds not subtracts time. Widening to 4–14 weeks with part-type breakdown reduces the risk of overclaiming precision while preserving the core pain-point assertion.

field_validation_question: What is your typical wait time, from placing a purchase order with the boiler OEM, to receiving: (a) replacement refractory tiles, (b) a new waterwall tube panel, (c) a grate/fuel-feed component, for a biomass package boiler installed in [Indonesia/Malaysia/Vietnam]?
